newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kao plans capital outlay of 70 bln yen in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Kao plans capital outlay of 70 bln yen in 1997/98.

text.p: Kao Corp, a leading maker of household products, said on Tuesday it plans capital investment of about 70 billion yen in 1997/98, down three billion yen from last business year.

Kao's executive vice president Shotaro Watanabe told a news conference the company's domestic capital investment would total 45 billion yen this business year, up 5.9 billion yen from 1996/97, while overseas capital investment would fall 8.9 billion yen to 25 billion yen.
Watanabe said domestic capital investment would be used to build and renovate distribution facilities and production facilities for new products.
Overseas capital investment would be used to build production facilities in Asian countries, including Vietnam, Indonesia and Thailand, he said.
He added that the company expects to post a depreciation loss on its facilities of 54 billion yen in 1997/98, down by 3.7 billion yen from last year.
It also expects its parent sales to rise by 1.1 percent to 704 billion yen in 1997/98.
If Kao had not reduced the price of products it sells to its sales affiliates by four percent in April, the company could have expected a 5.1 percent rise in sales, Watanabe said.
The company aims to increase its parent current profit by 4.4 percent in 1997/98, he said.
Watanabe added that quick action was required to improve the profitability of its information equipment business, which mainly operates in the United States.
